commit.message:
Add eth: paper and Lean 4 formalization of "A 2^o(n) Time Algorithm for 3-SAT" (#31)

Adds eth/, a self-contained Lake project (Lean v4.33.1, Mathlib v4.33.1), with the paper as eth/paper.pdf.
MainResults.lean states two propositions on Mathlib's Turing machines: that the Exponential Time Hypothesis
is false, and the paper's main theorem, that one deterministic machine counts, for every k, the satisfying
assignments of k-CNF formulas within the stated time bound. Solution.lean proves both from the files under
proof/, and comparator.json names them for Comparator. The only two sorry are in Challenge.lean, which states
the two theorems without proofs for that check. eth/README.md says how to check everything.
Adds the project's row to the table of the root README.

commit.message:
Add 3sum-apsp: formalization of "Truly Subquadratic 3SUM and Truly Subcubic APSP via Triangles in Sparse Lopsided Graphs" (#28)

* CI: take lean4export's vX.Y.0 tag when a Lean patch release has no tag of its own

For a project on a stable patch release vX.Y.Z (Z > 0), if
leanprover/lean4export has no tag vX.Y.Z, the check takes the tag vX.Y.0 and
builds it with the project's toolchain. Release candidates do not fall back.
A project whose exact tag exists is checked as before. The cache key of the
tools now includes the toolchain.

* Add 3sum-apsp: Lean 4 formalization accompanying "Truly Subquadratic 3SUM and Truly Subcubic APSP via Triangles in Sparse Lopsided Graphs"

A self-contained Lake project (Lean v4.33.1, Mathlib v4.33.1) in 3sum-apsp/.
EndStatement.lean states five headline claims about programs of a word RAM;
PaperStatements.lean states further results of the paper item by item;
ThreeSumApsp/ proves them. Two Comparator configurations list the compared
theorems. 3sum-apsp/README.md says what is proved and what is not.
Adds the project's row to the table of the root README.

commit.message:
Lay out zeta23 as a Palomar template project

Bring zeta23/ into the layout of PalomarRegistry/PalomarTemplate and the
Palomar CONTRIBUTING.md requirements, so it can be submitted with the
subdirectory as the selected project and zeta23/comparator.json as the
Comparator configuration.

- Move the Comparator layer from comparator/ to the project root:
  Challenge.lean, Solution.lean, ChallengeDeps.lean and their XiPrime
  submodules; config.json -> comparator.json, config-xiprime.json ->
  comparator-xiprime.json (both gain "definition_names": []);
  PrintAxioms audits -> scripts/. Lean sources are unchanged apart from
  path mentions in comment headers (comment-stripped sources are
  byte-identical to main).
- lakefile.toml: root-level Challenge/Solution/ChallengeDeps libraries
  (roots = [...]) instead of srcDir = "comparator"; Challenge and
  Solution join the default targets, as in the template.
- formalization.yaml: add the required project.description (registry
  abstract), the template's automation/cost fields, per-statement
  alignment notes, Palomar's source-type vocabulary (paper), updated
  paths, and a note that comparator.json is the submitted configuration.
- Add scripts/verify-comparator.sh (Comparator and lean4export pinned at
  their v4.33.0-rc2 tags, Landrun/NanoDa at the template's commits, with
  a config argument), scripts/landrun-wrapper.sh,
  scripts/validate-formalization.rb, test/, Gemfile, and docbuild/
  (doc-gen4 v4.33.0-rc2).
- Add .github/workflows/zeta23-ci.yml: metadata, licence, README link and
  Landrun-wrapper checks on every change; Lean build, docs and the
  pinned Comparator run on manual dispatch (they take hours). Add
  dependabot for actions.
- README: merge comparator/README.md, add a repository map, Palomar
  submission notes and the paper's arXiv title; AUDIT.md gets a revision
  note for the relayout; root README mentions the layout.

commit.message:
comparator: one statement set at the paper's constants; Challenge merged into a single Mathlib-only module

Merge the twelve statements of Challenge/Multiplicity.lean into Challenge.lean
and drop the ten strictly weaker Cauchy-Schwarz-form statements, so the
comparator states exactly the seventeen headline theorems A-E at the constants
stated in the paper (the set the top-level README's statement table lists).
Each dropped statement is implied by a kept one with the same counting function
and a strictly larger constant, so nothing previously claimed is lost; the
Cauchy-Schwarz theorems remain proved in the Zeta23 library.

Every kept theorem (doc comment and statement) is byte-identical to its
previous counterpart; no statement is reworded, no theorem renamed, so the
Solution delegations move verbatim. The merged Challenge.lean keeps the
complete inlined definition layer (see the preceding commit for why the block
must stay complete). Solution.lean takes the union of the two solution
modules' Zeta23 imports and keeps the single bridging lemma cStar_one_eq_cMT.

config-multiplicity.json, PrintAxioms/Multiplicity.lean. config.json lists the
seventeen names; PrintAxioms.lean prints them; AUDIT.md gains a revision note
recording the re-run checks on this revision's sources; both READMEs
updated (sorry count 33 -> 23 = 17 + 6).

commit.message:
comparator: inline the definition layer into the Challenge modules (Mathlib-only imports)

Palomar registry policy §2.4 requires the Challenge's transitive import
closure to contain no project-specific source (Lean core / Mathlib /
Tau Ceti only). Our Challenge modules imported the project file
ChallengeDeps.lean (resp. ChallengeDeps/XiPrime.lean).

This inlines the definition layer verbatim into each Challenge module,
so each Challenge module's ONLY import is Mathlib:

* Challenge.lean and Challenge/Multiplicity.lean: the 15 definitions of
  ChallengeDeps.lean, as a complete block;
* Challenge/XiPrime.lean: the 8 definitions of ChallengeDeps/XiPrime.lean.

The inlined definitions are character-for-character copies, wrapped in
an anonymous section reproducing the definition layer's exact open
context, so they elaborate to the same terms; the statement
declarations are byte-identical to before. Each module carries the
COMPLETE layer rather than only the constants its statements mention:
elaborating the layer as a whole keeps the auxiliary lemmas it
generates (e.g. N0star._proof_1, reused by later definitions) named
identically on the challenge and solution sides — comparator correctly
rejects a partial inline over exactly this. ChallengeDeps*.lean
continue to exist unchanged: Solution*.lean still import them, and the
comparator checks the inlined copies elaborate identically.

Verified: all three comparator configs (the repo's own config.json,
config-multiplicity.json, config-xiprime.json, enable_nanoda true,
unmodified) pass on this change — real landrun sandbox, nanoda second
kernel, comparator built from its v4.33.0-rc2 tag and lean4export at

commit.message:
comparator: trim ChallengeDeps.lean to the statements' dependency closure

Keep the trusted read for the comparator challenge as small as possible:
the four counting functions that no challenge statement depends on (N0,
Nsimple, N0L, NsimpleL -- kept until now for block-parity with the
Zeta23 statement layer) are removed, so ChallengeDeps.lean contains
exactly the definitions in the dependency closure of the challenge
statements, and every line an auditor of the statements reads is
load-bearing. README notes updated accordingly, and the layout
convention gains rule (6) making this minimality a requirement for
future topics.

No statement changes: Challenge.lean, Challenge/Multiplicity.lean and
Challenge/XiPrime.lean are unchanged byte for byte, and the removed
names were outside every statement's dependency closure, so the
comparator configurations are unaffected.

commit.message:
Add the zeros of ξ′ and the bandwidth-one ceiling

Extends the formalization by two groups of results cited in the paper (v4):

* Zeta23/XiPrime/ — the zeros of ξ′, the derivative of the completed zeta
  function: unconditionally at least 0.85838 of them (ordinates in (T,2T])
  are simple and on the critical line and at least 0.92919 are distinct
  (0.86864 / 0.93432 with the quartic window); all zeros of ξ′ lie in the
  open critical strip; Re ξ′/ξ > 0 on Re s ≥ 1. Comparator topic XiPrime
  (six trusted statements in comparator/Challenge/XiPrime.lean, with
  ChallengeDeps/XiPrime.lean, Solution/XiPrime.lean, config-xiprime.json,
  PrintAxioms/XiPrime.lean).

* Zeta23/PairCeiling/ — the stability inequality behind the remark on the
  optimality of the method (two integrations by parts) and its instance at
  an explicit 256-periodic law: every bandwidth-one certificate certifies a
  proportion of simple zeros at most 0.6818287 + 2.55e-6·(|r′(1)| + ∫|r″|).
  The one displayed hypothesis is EnclOK (the law's form factor lies in the
  recorded integer enclosures); the 255 row inequalities and the edge bound
  are checked in the kernel by decide. No trusted statement file;
  comparator/PrintAxioms/PairCeiling.lean is the axiom audit.

The ξ′ development uses later versions of 69 shared modules (PrimeSideA/B,
WeilEF, RvM, Taper, ThmD, ThmDE, ThmE, Assembly, Final, FinalMult,
ExplicitFormula, Chebyshev, ZeroSide/Mult, MV/Spacing, GammaFacts/Series,
Analytic/RectangleLogDeriv, Poisson/PaperFT, FromPNTPlus/StrongPNTPrefix):
same public statements — the trusted files comparator/ChallengeDeps.lean,
Challenge.lean and Challenge/Multiplicity.lean are unchanged byte for byte —
with newer proofs; in those files non-mathematical comments were removed.

Checks (Lean v4.33.0-rc2, Mathlib 51e6992efd06): lake build (default target
+ all comparator libraries) green; #print axioms on the 15 + 12 + 6
comparator statements and on the PairCeiling theorems: the three standard
axioms only (LawN256_check: propext; LawN256_edge: none); sorry only in the
trusted challenge files (15 + 12 + 6 declarations); comparator okay on
config.json, config-multiplicity.json, config-xiprime.json. See AUDIT.md.
